tasks.short: Test materials and file the accepted analysis.

steps.what: Conduct materials analysis using tools and equipment.
Keep applying engineering knowledge to the analysis.

tasks.design: The technician conducts the materials analysis with the tools and equipment and keeps applying engineering knowledge. They accept the result. {DOCS} files only that version. A reading they did not take is not entered. Nothing runs the test.
tasks.previous_blocker: Readings they had already taken were copied into the file later.
tasks.enabler_now: A result they have already accepted can be filed without retyping the readings.
tasks.still_hard: What the test shows stays with the technician who used the tools.
tasks.human_edge: The technician tests. A file does not.
tasks.altitude: The test and the analysis stay in full. Only filing the accepted analysis is shorter.

reach.task: Read the analysis the technician accepted
reach.learn: The supervisor does not run the test

evidence.claim: A materials test is the technician's work with the tools. A reading they did not take is not entered.

assumptions: The workflow starts when a sample is in front of the technician and ends when the accepted analysis is filed. The technician conducts the test. A reading they did not take is not entered.
The fields are sample id, the reading they took, and the result they accept. The technician produces them. A reading they did not take is not entered.
The prior classes this task as human. The steps agree the test stays. Filing the accepted analysis is the part that moves.
unknowns: Whether the tools already show a reading the technician must still accept.
Which tests the office will not file until a second sample is run.
research_questions: Do the tools already show a reading the technician must still accept?
Which tests will the office not file until a second sample is run?

tasks.short: Estimate installation costs and file them.

steps.what: Develop plans for installation of systems.
Estimate costs for utilization of facilities.
Accept the construction of the structures.

tasks.design: The technician develops the plans for installation of systems, estimates the costs for utilization of facilities, and accepts the construction of the structures. {DOCS} only opens quantities they already marked, then files the costs they accepted. The sheet does not choose the estimate. A price they did not accept is not filed.
tasks.previous_blocker: Marked quantities were copied again before they could estimate.
tasks.enabler_now: Quantities they have already marked can be opened in the estimate.
tasks.still_hard: What the installation should cost stays with the technician.
tasks.human_edge: The technician estimates. A quantity list does not.
tasks.altitude: Developing the plans and estimating the costs stay in full. Only opening marked quantities and filing the accepted costs are shorter.

reach.learn: The estimator does not set this estimate

evidence.claim: A quantity can be calculated from dimensions the technician has marked. A figure they did not mark is not calculated.
A stated price can be shown. Which price applies is the technician's estimate.

assumptions: The workflow starts when installation quantities are marked and ends when the accepted costs are filed. The technician develops the plan and estimates. The sheet does not choose the cost.
The fields are system name, the quantity they marked, and the cost they estimate. The quantity sheet produces the marks. The technician produces the cost. A cost they did not accept is not filed.
The prior classes this task as amplify. The steps agree the estimate stays. The open and the filing are the parts that move.
unknowns: Whether installation quantities are already marked before the estimate starts.
Which facilities the office will not price from a marked quantity alone.
research_questions: Are installation quantities already marked before the estimate starts?
Which facilities will the office not price from a marked quantity alone?

tasks.short: Develop project budgets and file them.

steps.what: Read prices for the project activities.
Develop project budgets from those activities.
Keep estimating the cost of project activities.

tasks.design: The technician develops the project budgets and keeps estimating the cost of the project activities, then accepts the budgets. {DOCS} only shows published prices, then files the budgets they accepted. The price list does not choose the budget.
tasks.previous_blocker: A published price was looked up again before they could estimate the activity.
tasks.enabler_now: A price the office already published can be shown beside the activity.
tasks.still_hard: What the activity should cost in this budget stays with the technician.
tasks.human_edge: The technician estimates. A price list does not.
tasks.altitude: Developing the budgets and estimating the activities stay in full. Only showing published prices and filing the accepted budgets are shorter.

reach.task: Read the budget the technician accepted
reach.learn: The supervisor does not estimate the activities

evidence.claim: A stated price can be shown. Which price applies is the technician's estimate.

assumptions: The workflow starts when project activities need a budget and ends when the accepted budget is filed. The technician estimates. The price list does not choose the figure.

The fields are the activity name and the published price. The price list produces the published amount. The technician produces the budget figure. If the list has no row, they estimate it themselves and the lookup stays unused.
The prior classes this task as human. The steps agree the estimating stays. The lookup and the filing are the parts that move.
unknowns: Whether a published price exists for every project activity.
Which activities the office estimates with no published price.
research_questions: Does a published price exist for every project activity?
Which activities does the office estimate with no published price?

tasks.short: Survey the sites and file the accepted notes.

steps.what: Conduct field surveys of the project sites.
Locate new sites during the field surveys.
Analyze details of the project sites.

tasks.design: The technician conducts the field surveys, locates new sites, analyzes the details, and accepts the surveys. {DOCS} files only the notes they accepted after the survey. Nothing locates a site and nothing analyzes the ground. A point they did not observe is not filed.
tasks.previous_blocker: Notes they had already taken in the field were copied into the file later.
tasks.enabler_now: A survey note they have already accepted can be filed without retyping it.
tasks.still_hard: Where the site is, and what the details mean, stay with the technician in the field.
tasks.human_edge: The technician surveys. A file does not.
tasks.altitude: The surveys, the locating, and the analysis stay in full. Only filing the accepted survey notes is shorter.

reach.task: Use the survey the technician accepted
reach.learn: The designer does not locate the site

evidence.claim: A site inspection is the technician's observation. The file is the note they accepted after the visit. It is not a generated finding.

assumptions: The workflow starts when a field survey is ordered and ends when the accepted survey is filed. The technician conducts it. A point they did not observe is not filed.
The fields are site id, the point they located, and the detail they analyzed. The technician produces them in the field. A point they did not observe is not filed.
The prior classes this task as human. The steps agree the surveys stay. Filing the accepted notes is the part that moves.
unknowns: Whether the office already holds a prior survey of the project sites.
Which new sites the office will not accept until the technician has stood on them.
research_questions: Does the office already hold a prior survey of the project sites?
Which new sites will the office not accept until the technician has stood on them?
